2607.13425.title: Data-Efficient Adaptation of LLMs via Attention Head Reweighting
2607.13425.paper_summary: Learning effectively from limited data is critical in domains like security where labeled examples are scarce. Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated some capabilities for data-efficient learning, especially through parameter-efficient adaptation methods, but continue to struggle when faced with few samples for difficult tasks. To meet this challenge, we propose Attention Head Reweighting (AHR), a data-efficient method that adapts LLMs to new text-classification tasks by learning only a single scalar per attention head. This drastically reduces the number of parameters that need to be learned by making use of the functional specialization of individual attention heads. Experiments on diverse open-source text classification datasets show that AHR can outperform standard baselines like LoRA when learning from limited samples, despite having 200-1000x fewer trainable parameters, as our AHR only modifies ~0.0001% of the model's parameters. In addition, our learned weights are easy to interpret and can be analyzed to better understand the mechanisms and attention heads responsible for in-context learning abilities in LLMs.
2607.13425.paper_summary_zh: 有效地從有限數據中學習在安全等標記範例稀缺的領域中至關重要。大型語言模型（LLMs）已展示出某些數據高效學習的能力，特別是通過參數高效的適應方法，但在面對難度較大的任務時，仍然面臨少量樣本的挑戰。為了應對這一挑戰，我們提出了注意力頭重加權（AHR），這是一種數據高效的方法，通過僅為每個注意力頭學習一個標量來將LLMs適應於新的文本分類任務。這大幅減少了需要學習的參數數量，利用了個別注意力頭的功能專業化。在多樣的開源文本分類數據集上的實驗顯示，AHR在從有限樣本中學習時能超越標準基準，如LoRA，儘管我們的AHR僅修改了模型參數的約0.0001%，並且訓練可調參數少了200-1000倍。此外，我們學習的權重易於解釋，並且可以分析以更好地理解在LLMs中負責上下文學習能力的機制和注意力頭。
